subject: Post-call: Ops & model deep-dive timebox and stakeholder confirmation
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Lee <simon@pioneer.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Ops & model deep-dive timebox and stakeholder confirmation

Hi Simon — thanks again for a productive discovery call today. Quick recap and next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Goal for the next call: 60–90 minute technical deep dive (TDX) with your infra and ML engineering teams to walk through integration surface area, performance targets, and security controls.

2) Proposed agenda (we can tighten based on your ask):
   - 5m: introductions & success criteria
   - 15m: high-level architecture & integration patterns (routing, model variants)
   - 20m: runtime performance (latency SLOs, batching, KV/prefix caching)
   - 20m: security/compliance + data flow (SOC 2 scoping, encryption, audit logs)
   - 15m: capacity & fallbacks (Dedicated vs Hosted routing)
   - 10m: Q&A + next action items

3) Time options (all PT):
   - Thursday, Dec 3: 10:00–11:30 (60–90m)
   - Friday, Dec 4: 09:00–10:30 (60–90m)
   - Monday, Dec 7: 14:00–15:30 (60–90m)

Can you confirm which slot works and who from your side should join? You mentioned bringing your infra lead — please CC them so we can include any specific artifacts.

Prep items we’ll send ahead: lightweight prep checklist (env examples, sample payload sizes, representative prompts/seq lengths). I’ll attach the checklist once we lock a time. 

If you prefer a Calendly/Teams invite, we can send a one-click link — whatever’s easiest for your calendar team.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: (will attach tdx-prep-checklist.pdf after slot confirmed)

Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 18:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Ops & model deep-dive timebox and stakeholder confirmation

Thanks Ava — great recap.

We can take the TDX next week. Priorities from our side: SOC 2 data flow mapping and how you handle persistent KV caches (we have constraints around PHI), plus a short discussion on encryption-at-rest and in-transit key management.

Preferred slots for us: Dec 3 is tight due to an exec review, so Dec 4 09:00–10:30 PT works well. I'll loop in our infra lead Jared (cc’d). He may want to talk about network egress, VPC peering, and any on-prem appliance options.

Could you include a short list of the RFC-style artifacts you need ahead of time (sample payload sizes, expected concurrent sessions)? If you have a Calendly link that sets the invite directly with your SEs, that makes life easier — otherwise we’ll accept the invite.

Simon Lee
Head of Product, Pioneer Health
simon@pioneer.ai

Ava / Grace — quick internal note on how we should run the TDX for Pioneer: 

- Focus areas to prepare:
  * KV/prefix cache behavior and isolation for PHI-like workloads
  * Quantization and perf tradeoffs (FP16 vs 4-bit options) and expected token throughput on Dedicated pools
  * Network egress patterns, VPC peering options, and KMS integration for envelope keys
  * Small demo: 2-minute perf demo showing batch size impact on p99 latency (we can record short clip in case they want it pasted in chat)

- Slot confirmation: Dec 4, 09:00–10:30 PT — works for me. I’ll be the primary SE on the call and will bring telemetry examples. Grace, can you bring the renewal/contract touchpoints so we can answer any procurement timeline questions?

- Prep attachments I’ll circulate: tdx-prep-checklist.pdf (checklist of artifacts & sample sizes), small perf-run screenshots, and a short network diagram. I’ll attach the checklist now.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
